title: Eyes of Wakanda
description: Explores Wakanda across different time periods, showing how its influence stretches beyond what we've seen in the films. Follows the Wakandan War Dogs on dangerous missions to recover stolen Vibranium before it can change the course of history. An animated style makes it feel different from the usual MCU. Expands the lore of Wakanda, including its traditions and its secret role in world events.

title: Spider-Noir
description: Follows Ben Reilly, a private investigator and former masked hero known as The Spider. A dangerous investigation forces him back into the superhero life and New York's criminal underworld. His wartime past reveals that his powers originated during World War I after exposure to German experiments involving genetically altered soldiers and a spider-like mutant. A darker live-action Spider-Man story blending 1930s crime noir, organised crime, detective storytelling, and themes of redemption, grief, identity and responsibility.

title: Captain America: The First Avenger
description: The origin story of Steve Rogers, a weak but determined man who becomes the world's first super-soldier. It blends wartime with superhero action, introducing Captain America as a symbol of courage and sacrifice. Introduces the Tesseract, one of the MCU's most important artifacts. Establishes characters and organisations that become important later, including Hydra and the beginnings of S.H.I.E.L.D.

title: Agent Carter: One Shot
description: Follows Peggy Carter as she struggles to prove herself in a male-dominated post-war world while secretly carrying out dangerous missions for the SSR. Shows that Peggy is a skilled agent in her own right rather than just Captain America's love interest. Expands the early history of the Strategic Scientific Reserve (SSR), the organisation that eventually leads to the creation of S.H.I.E.L.D. A short character piece that adds emotional weight to Peggy's story and shows the beginnings of the intelligence world behind the Avengers.

title: Agent Carter: Season One
description: Follows Peggy Carter working for the SSR in post-war America, secretly investigating threats while being underestimated by her male colleagues. Similarly to 'Agent Carter: One Shot', the show expands Peggy from a supporting character into a fully developed hero, showing her intelligence, combat skills, determination, and independence. Introduces key MCU concepts like Howard Stark's inventions, early experiments, and the connection between science, espionage, and future organisations. Deepens the foundations of the MCU's spy world by exploring the SSR and the early origins of S.H.I.E.L.D.

title: Agent Carter: Season Two
flashbacks: pre-World War II, World War II (1939 - 1945)
description: Follows Peggy Carter's move to Los Angeles and investigation of a mysterious case involving a strange energy source and a dangerous conspiracy. Expands the MCU's science and supernatural side, exploring unusual experiments and threats beyond normal espionage. Continues Peggy's journey as she fights to be recognised as one of the SSR's top agents while navigating the changing post-war world. Further develops connections between the SSR, Howard Stark, and the foundations of the future intelligence networks of the MCU.

title: X-Men: First Class
description: Explores the origins of the X-Men, showing how Charles Xavier and Erik Lehnsherr (Magneto) went from allies and friends to ideological rivals. Introduces the early mutant community, showing how mutants first began operating in a world that fears and misunderstands them. Blends superhero action with Cold War espionage, as the mutants become involved in a global crisis involving nuclear tensions. Reimagines the history of the X-Men universe, establishing the foundations of the mutant conflict, Charles' school, and Magneto's future path.

title: Fantastic Four: First Steps
description: Introduces Marvel's first family: Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm, as they become the Fantastic Four after a scientific mission changes their lives forever. Takes place in a retro-futuristic world where the team are already established heroes. Brings cosmic Marvel into focus by introducing threats beyond Earth, including Galactus. Establishes a new version of the Fantastic Four within the MCU's multiverse, setting up their eventual connection to the wider Marvel universe, and provides a fresh starting point for Marvel's most famous superhero family, focusing less on their origin and more on their relationships, legacy, and place in the universe.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
description: Follows Wolverine as he is sent back in time to prevent a catastrophic future where mutants and humans are hunted by unstoppable Sentinels. Brings together the original X-Men cast and the younger 'First Class' cast, connecting two generations of mutant stories. Explores the complicated relationship between Charles Xavier and Magneto, showing how their choices shape the future of mutant-kind. One of the most important X-Men films for the timeline, as its events dramatically alter the mutant universe and create a new future (however, it does make the timeline slightly confusing!).

title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
description: Explores the early life of Logan (Wolverine), including his childhood, his relationship with his brother Victor Creed (Sabretooth), and the events that shaped him. Shows Logan's time as a soldier and member of Team X before he becomes the lone, mysterious mutant known as Wolverine. Introduces important elements of Wolverine's history, including the Weapon X programme that transforms his skeleton into adamantium. Presents some continuity issues but provides a deeper look at Wolverine's origins and trauma, exploring his rage, loss, and identity struggles.

title: X-Men: Apocalypse
description: Follows the young X-Men as they face Apocalypse, one of the world's first and most powerful mutants, who awakens after thousands of years and seeks to completely reshape humanity. Expands mutant mythology by introducing one of the oldest and strongest beings in X-Men history, along with his four Horsemen. Includes the younger versions of Charles Xavier, Magneto, Mystique, and Beast as they deal with the consequences of the events from 'Days of Future Past'. Develops other key characters including Cyclops, Jean Grey, Nightcrawler, and Storm, showing the next generation of X-Men coming together. Explores the idea of whether humanity deserves saving, and what happens when the most powerful mutant alive challenges the world.

title: X-Men: Dark Phoenix
description: Follows Jean Grey as a cosmic force known as the Phoenix dramatically amplifies her already immense telepathic abilities, forcing the X-Men to confront one of their own. Explores Jean's struggle with power, identity, and control as the Phoenix begins to change her into one of the most dangerous beings in the universe. Expands the cosmic side of the X-Men universe, introducing alien influences and showing that mutant threats extend far beyond Earth.

title: Captain Marvel
description: Follows Carol Danvers, a former Air Force pilot who gains cosmic abilities and becomes one of the most powerful heroes in the Marvel universe. Explores the origins of Captain Marvel while revealing the hidden history of the Kree-Skrull conflict and Earth's place in a much larger galaxy. Takes inspiration from 1990s sci-fi and spy thrillers, showing a younger Nick Fury and the early days of S.H.I.E.L.D. before the Avengers existed.

title: Blade
description: Follows Blade, a half-vampire, half-human warrior who uses his abilities to hunt vampires and protect humanity from the creatures hiding in the shadows. Explores the hidden world of vampires, introducing a more brutal and mature side of Marvel that exists outside the usual superhero formula.

title: X-Men
description: Introduces the world of mutants, where people born with extraordinary abilities are feared by society and forced to fight for acceptance. Follows Wolverine and Rogue as they become involved with Professor Charles Xavier's X-Men, a team dedicated to protecting both mutants and humans. Establishes the central conflict between Charles Xavier's dream of peaceful coexistence and Magneto's belief that mutants must defend themselves from humanity. Introduces X-Men characters, including Cyclops, Jean Grey, Storm, Mystique, and Magneto, creating the foundation for the entire X-Men film universe.

title: Blade Two
description: Continues the story of Blade, the vampire hunter who must team up with his enemies when a new breed of terrifying creatures threatens both humans and vampires. Expands vampire mythology by introducing the Reapers, a powerful mutation that creates a threat unlike anything Blade has faced before. Forces Blade into an uneasy alliance with the vampire world, exploring the idea that even enemies may need to work together against a greater danger.

title: Madame Web
description: Follows Cassandra Webb, a paramedic who develops the ability to see possible futures and must protect three young women who are connected to a Spider-Man-related prophecy. Adds background to the world surrounding Spider-related heroes, including early hints at how future figures could emerge. A different kind of superhero story that focuses on fate, destiny, and protecting the next generation rather than traditional superhero battles.

title: Spider-Man
description: Follows Peter Parker, a gifted but ordinary teenager who gains spider-like abilities after a genetically altered spider bite and must learn that great power comes with great responsibility. Explores Peter's transformation from an awkward outsider into Spider-Man, balancing his new abilities with school, relationships, and personal loss. Introduces characters including Mary Jane Watson, and Norman Osborn (Green Goblin). A film that helped redefine comic book movies, combining action, heart, and the emotional struggles that make Spider-Man one of Marvel's most relatable heroes.

title: X2: X-Men United
description: Continues the story of the X-Men as tensions between humans and mutants escalate following the first film. Explores Wolverine's past further, revealing more about the Weapon X programme and the experiments that created him. Forces the X-Men and Magneto's Brotherhood to cooperate when a greater threat puts all mutants at risk.

title: Daredevil
description: Follows Matt Murdock, a blind lawyer by day who uses his heightened senses to become Daredevil, a vigilante protecting Hell's Kitchen at night. Focuses on crime, corruption, and justice rather than world-ending threats. Shows Matt's struggle between his Catholic beliefs, his desire for justice, and the violent methods he uses as Daredevil. Introduces key characters including Wilson Fisk (Kingpin), Bullseye, and Elektra.

title: Spider-Man Two
description: Continues Peter Parker's journey as he struggles to balance his life as Spider-Man with his responsibilities, relationships, and personal sacrifices. Explores the emotional cost of being a hero, as Peter questions whether he can continue carrying the burden of protecting others. Introduces Dr. Otto Octavius (Doctor Octopus), a scientist whose tragic transformation creates one of Spider-Man's biggest villains. Expands Peter's world by developing his relationships with Mary Jane, Aunt May, and the people affected by his choices as a hero.

title: Blade Trinity
description: Follows Blade as he becomes hunted by both humans and vampires after being framed for a series of crimes, forcing him to work with a new generation of vampire hunters. Introduces Dracula (known as Drake), one of the oldest and most powerful vampires in existence, and the Nightstalkers, a group of human vampire hunters including Hannibal King and Abigail Whistler, who bring a new dynamic to Blade's mission.

title: Elektra
description: Follows Elektra Natchios, a skilled assassin who must protect a young girl with a mysterious connection to a powerful ancient organisation. Explores Elektra's character beyond her role in Daredevil, focusing on her trauma, redemption, and struggle between being a killer and a protector. Introduces The Hand, a secretive group of assassins connected to the wider Daredevil mythology.

title: Fantastic Four
description: Follows Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm as a scientific mission exposes them to cosmic radiation, giving them incredible abilities and transforming them into Marvel's first family. Introduces the Fantastic Four as a team of heroes who must learn to adapt to their powers. Explores the contrast between scientific discovery and responsibility, especially through Reed Richards' genius and obsession with solving problems. Introduces Victor Von Doom, a brilliant scientist and former ally whose own ambition and resentment turn him into the villain Doctor Doom.

title: X-Men: The Last Stand
description: Follows the X-Men as a "mutant cure" is introduced, forcing mutants to question whether their abilities are a gift, a burden, or something that should be removed. Explores the growing divide between Professor Xavier's dream of peaceful coexistence and Magneto's belief that mutants must fight back against humanity. Introduces the Phoenix storyline, showing Jean Grey's immense power and the consequences of a force she can no longer fully control.

title: Fantastic Four: Rise of The Silver Surfer
description: Follows the Fantastic Four as they encounter the Silver Surfer, a cosmic being whose arrival warns of an approaching threat capable of destroying worlds. Introduces Galactus, one of the universe's most powerful entities and one of the Fantastic Four's greatest comic-book foes. Explores the team's struggle between being superheroes, public figures, and a family trying to live normal lives.

title: Ghost Rider
description: Follows Johnny Blaze, a motorcycle stunt rider who makes a supernatural deal with the Devil (Mephistopheles) that transforms him into the Ghost Rider, the spirit of vengeance forced to battle evil. Explores Johnny's struggle between his human identity and his role as a supernatural weapon bound to a dark force.

title: Spider-Man Three
description: Follows Peter Parker as he faces new threats while struggling with fame, relationships, and the darker parts of himself after encountering the Venom symbiote. Introduces the black Spider-Man suit and explores how the symbiote amplifies Peter's anger, pride, and desire for revenge. Expands Peter's rogues' gallery by introducing Sandman, Venom, and Harry Osborn's transformation into the Hob Goblin.

title: Iron Man
description: Introduces Tony Stark, a billionaire weapons manufacturer whose life changes after being captured and forced to confront the consequences of his own creations. Follows Tony's transformation from a selfish weapons genius into Iron Man, as he builds his first suit of armour and becomes a true hero. Establishes the foundation of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, introducing the first major hero of the Avengers era. Introduces key elements of the MCU including S.H.I.E.L.D., Nick Fury, and a connected universe of heroes.

title: The Incredible Hulk
description: Follows Bruce Banner as he searches for a cure to the condition that transforms him into the Hulk while staying one step ahead of the military determined to capture him. Explores the consequences of failed super-soldier research. Introduces Emil Blonsky, whose pursuit of power transforms him into the Abomination. A tense action thriller that explores Bruce Banner's struggle to control the monster within while proving that true strength comes from mastering, not embracing, his rage.

title: Iron Man Two
description: Continues Tony Stark's journey as the world learns his secret identity, forcing him to deal with fame, government pressure, and the responsibility of being Iron Man. Introduces new threats including Ivan Vanko (Whiplash), who uses similar technology to Tony's armour to seek revenge against the Stark family. Introduces Natasha Romanoff (Black Widow), building towards the formation of the Avengers. Deepens Tony's character by exploring his legacy, and his relationship with his father Howard Stark.

title: A Funny Thing Happened On The Way To Thor’s Hammer: One Shot
description: Follows Phil Coulson as he travels to New Mexico to investigate the discovery of Thor's hammer, Mjolnir. Shows Coulson's everyday life as a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, highlighting his quick thinking, professionalism, and ability to handle unexpected situations. Provides a comedic look at Coulson's character while expanding his role as one of the MCU's key figures.

title: Thor
description: Follows Thor, the arrogant heir to Asgard's throne, who is banished to Earth and forced to learn humility, responsibility, and what it truly means to be worthy. Expands the MCU beyond Earth by introducing Asgard, the Nine Realms, and the cosmic / mystical side of Marvel. Introduces key characters including Loki, Odin, Jane Foster, Heimdall, and the wider Asgardian mythology. Introduces Mjolnir and establishes the concept of worthiness, one of the most important ideas connected to Thor's character. Expands the Avengers setup by introducing another major hero and showing S.H.I.E.L.D.'s involvement with powerful beings beyond Earth.

title: The Consultant: One Shot
description: Follows S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Phil Coulson and Jasper Sitwell as they carry out a seemingly routine assignment that has unexpected consequences for the future of the Avengers Initiative. Gives a funny behind-the-scenes look at S.H.I.E.L.D.'s methods, showing that not every mission is solved through action alone. Directly connects Iron Man 2 and The Incredible Hulk, explaining why certain characters and events unfold the way they do in the early MCU.

title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
description: Follows Johnny Blaze as he struggles to control the Ghost Rider's curse while being drawn into a mission to protect a young boy from a demonic force. Expands the supernatural side of Marvel, exploring the true nature of the Spirit of Vengeance and the ongoing battle between heaven and hell. Shows a darker, more unstable Ghost Rider, whose powers have become increasingly difficult for Johnny to control.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
description: Follows Peter Parker as he discovers the truth behind his parents' disappearance while becoming Spider-Man after being bitten by a genetically altered spider. Reimagines Spider-Man's origin story, focusing more on Peter's intelligence, scientific abilities, and search for answers about his family's past. Introduces Dr. Curt Connors (The Lizard), a former partner of Peter's father whose experiments with regeneration lead to a dangerous transformation. Establishes a new version of Spider-Man's world, including Gwen Stacy, Captain George Stacy, and a different interpretation of Peter's early years as a hero. A fresh take on Spider-Man that explores identity, loss, and responsibility while beginning a new cinematic universe separate from the Raimi trilogy.

title: The Avengers
description: Brings together Earth's Mightiest Heroes for the first time as Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye unite to stop a global threat. Follows Loki's invasion of Earth using the Tesseract and an alien army, forcing the heroes to overcome their differences and work as a team. A landmark superhero crossover that proved interconnected cinematic universes could work, setting the foundation for the future of the MCU.

title: Item 47: One Shot
description: Follows a couple who discover a Chitauri weapon left behind after the Battle of New York and decide to use it for their own purposes. Explores the aftermath of the Battle of New York from the perspective of ordinary civilians, showing how alien technology begins spreading into the wider world. Introduces S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Jasper Sitwell and Benjamin "Benny" Pollak as they track down the stolen Chitauri weapon. Expands the consequences of the Avengers' first major battle, showing that the invasion created new problems beyond the immediate threat.

title: Iron Man Three
description: Follows Tony Stark as he struggles with the psychological aftermath of the Battle of New York while facing a mysterious terrorist known as the Mandarin. Explores Tony's anxiety, trauma, and dependence on his Iron Man suits. Introduces the Extremis programme, a powerful experimental technology with dangerous consequences.

title: All Hail The King: One Shot
description: Revisits Trevor Slattery in prison after the events of Iron Man 3, where an interview uncovers surprising truths about the identity of the Mandarin. Expands on one of the MCU's most controversial twists. Reveals that the "Mandarin" is far more than just the fake terrorist seen in Iron Man 3, laying the groundwork for future MCU stories. An important one shot that recontextualises Iron Man 3 and pays off years later in Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.

title: Agents Of Shield: Season One, Episodes 1 - 7
description: Follows Agent Phil Coulson as he assembles a small team of S.H.I.E.L.D. agents to investigate unusual cases involving advanced technology, superhuman abilities, and mysterious phenomena around the world. Introduces the core team, including Skye, Melinda May, Grant Ward, Leo Fitz, and Jemma Simmons. Expands the MCU by exploring the everyday work of S.H.I.E.L.D., showing how the organisation deals with the aftermath of superhero battles and emerging threats that don't make the headlines.

title: The Wolverine
description: Follows Logan as he travels to Japan, where he is offered the chance to become mortal and must confront his past, his grief, and what it truly means to live without his healing abilities. Explores Wolverine's vulnerability like never before, forcing him to rely on his instincts and determination rather than his near-invincibility. Introduces a new cast of allies and enemies while diving into Japan's criminal underworld, samurai traditions, and honour-based conflicts. Continues Logan's story after the original X-Men trilogy, showing the lasting emotional impact of previous events and setting up his future within the X-Men universe.

title: Thor: The Dark World
description: Follows Thor as he battles the Dark Elves to stop an ancient force known as the Aether from plunging the universe into darkness. Expands the cosmic side of the MCU, exploring the Nine Realms, the Convergence, and the history of Asgard long before Thor's time. Introduces the Aether, later revealed to be the Reality Stone. Develops Thor and Loki's complicated relationship while further connecting Asgard's story to the wider MCU.

title: Agents of Shield: Season One, Episodes 8 - 16
description: Continues Coulson's team’s investigations as S.H.I.E.L.D. deals with the consequences of alien technology, enhanced individuals, and threats emerging after the events of The Avengers. Expands the mystery surrounding Coulson's return after the Battle of New York. Develops the team's individual stories, including Skye's search for answers about her past and the growing trust between the members of Coulson's team.

title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
description: Follows Steve Rogers as he struggles to adapt to the modern world while uncovering a conspiracy that threatens the very foundations of S.H.I.E.L.D. and global security. Introduces the Winter Soldier, a mysterious assassin with a personal connection to Steve's past.

title: Agents of Shield: Season One, Episodes 17 - 22
description: Continues Coulson's team’s mission as the collapse of S.H.I.E.L.D. forces them to question everything they know, including who they can trust. Directly explores the aftermath of Captain America: The Winter Soldier, showing the consequences of Hydra's infiltration of S.H.I.E.L.D. from the perspective of the agents on the ground. Forces Coulson and his team to operate independently as they become fugitives, reshaping their understanding of loyalty, friendship, and what S.H.I.E.L.D. truly stands for. Resolves major mysteries from the first half of the season, including the truth behind Coulson's resurrection and the secrets surrounding his survival after the Battle of New York.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man Two
description: Follows Peter Parker as he continues balancing his life as Spider-Man while uncovering more about his parents' past and facing new threats in New York. Introduces Max Dillon, who transforms into Electro after an accident, becoming a powerful enemy with a personal connection to Spider-Man. Expands Peter's rogues' gallery by introducing Harry Osborn and setting up his transformation into the Green Goblin, while also teasing the creation of the Sinister Six. Explores Peter and Gwen Stacy's relationship, as Peter struggles with the promise he made to protect her and the dangers that come with being Spider-Man. Continues the mystery surrounding Oscorp and Peter's parents, expanding this version of Spider-Man's universe beyond just one hero and his villains.

title: Guardians of The Galaxy
description: Introduces the cosmic side of the MCU by following Peter Quill (Star-Lord), a human abducted from Earth as a child who becomes a space outlaw. Brings together an unlikely group of heroes: Star-Lord, Gamora, Rocket, Groot, and Drax, who must work together to stop a powerful weapon from falling into the wrong hands. Introduces the Power Stone, one of the six Infinity Stones, and reveals its connection to the larger threat building across the universe. Expands Marvel's cosmic mythology by introducing planets, alien civilisations, the Nova Corps, the Kree, and major figures like Thanos and Ronan the Accuser.

title: I Am Groot: Season One
description: Follows Groot’s regrowth between Guardians Of The Galaxy Volume One And Guardians Of The Galaxy Volume Two. Follows Baby Groot as he explores the universe, encountering new creatures, planets, and unusual situations. Expands more on Groot's childhood adventures and his life as a small member of the Guardians. A fun collection of short stories showing the playful side of one of the MCU's most beloved cosmic characters.

title: I Am Groot: Season Two
description: Follows Groot’s regrowth between Guardians Of The Galaxy Volume One And Guardians Of The Galaxy Volume Two. Continues following Baby Groot as he explores the universe, encountering new creatures, planets, and unusual situations. Expands more on Groot's childhood adventures and his life as a small member of the Guardians. A fun collection of short stories showing the playful side of one of the MCU's most beloved cosmic characters.

title: Guardians of The Galaxy: Volume Two
description: Follows the Guardians as they continue their adventures across the galaxy while struggling with their new reputation as heroes. Explores Peter Quill's search for answers about his parentage after meeting Ego, a powerful celestial being who claims to be his father. Introduces Ego the Living Planet, revealing more about the nature of Celestials. Further develops the Guardians as a family, focusing on their relationships, personal histories, and the bonds they form with each other. Expands the stories of Rocket, Yondu, and Nebula, exploring their pasts, trauma, and complicated relationships with their respective families. Additionally introduces the character Mantis.

title: Daredevil: Season One
description: Follows Matt Murdock, a blind lawyer by day and masked vigilante by night, as he fights to protect Hell's Kitchen from rising crime and corruption. Explores a darker, street-level side of Marvel, focusing on organised crime, morality, justice, and the consequences of violence. Introduces Wilson Fisk (Kingpin), a powerful crime boss whose vision for rebuilding Hell's Kitchen puts him directly against Daredevil. Develops Matt's internal conflict between his Catholic faith, his desire to help people, and the brutal methods required to take on criminals.

title: Jessica Jones: Season One
description: Follows Jessica Jones, a private investigator, as she attempts to rebuild her life while confronting the trauma of her past. Explores the darker psychological side of being a superpowered person, focusing on control, manipulation, survival, and the lasting effects of abuse. Introduces Kilgrave (the Purple Man), a dangerous individual with the ability to control people's minds, forcing Jessica to confront the person responsible for her trauma.

title: Fant4stic
description: Follows Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm as they gain extraordinary abilities after travelling to an alternate dimension during a scientific experiment. Explores a darker, more science-fiction-focused version of the Fantastic Four, focusing on experimentation, discovery, and the consequences of playing with unknown forces. Introduces a new version of Victor Von Doom, whose transformation into a powerful being makes him a threat to the team and the world around them. Acts as a reboot of the Fantastic Four franchise rather than a continuation of the 2005 films, creating a separate version of the team's origins. A more serious and grounded take on Marvel's First Family, attempting to reimagine the team with a heavier sci-fi and body-horror influence.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Two, Episodes 1 - 19
description: Continues Coulson's team’s mission as the remnants of S.H.I.E.L.D. attempt to rebuild after Hydra's infiltration and the organisation's collapse. Explores the discovery of ancient alien symbols and the mysterious Kree influence connected to Coulson's transformation, expanding the MCU's cosmic mythology. Introduces new enhanced individuals known as Inhumans, beginning to reveal a larger world of people with extraordinary abilities existing outside the Avengers. Shows S.H.I.E.L.D. operating in the shadows, with Coulson building a new version of the organisation while dealing with distrust from governments and former allies. Develops the conflict between different factions within S.H.I.E.L.D., exploring loyalty, leadership, and what the organisation should become after Hydra's betrayal.

title: The Avengers: Age of Ultron
description: Follows the Avengers as they attempt to create a global defence system using artificial intelligence, only for their creation, Ultron, to become a threat to humanity. Introduces Ultron, an advanced AI created by Tony Stark and Bruce Banner that develops its own interpretation of peace and decides humanity itself is the problem. Introduces Wanda Maximoff (Scarlet Witch) and Pietro Maximoff (Quicksilver), two enhanced individuals whose abilities and history connect to the wider world of superhumans. Expands the Avengers team by introducing Vision and showing the evolution of Earth's Mightiest Heroes after their first major battle. Has major consequences for the MCU, including the creation of new Avengers, and the rise of international concerns over superheroes. A pivotal story that explores the dangers of unchecked power and technology.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Two, Episodes 20 - 22
description: Continues Coulson's rebuilt S.H.I.E.L.D. as the team faces the consequences of the emergence of the Inhumans and the growing tensions between different factions. Expands the Inhuman storyline, exploring the conflict between humans and enhanced individuals while revealing more about their origins and abilities. Shows S.H.I.E.L.D. dealing with threats on a larger scale, connecting the organisation's work to the wider world of enhanced beings and global security. Develops the personal journeys of Coulson's team, with major choices and consequences shaping the future of S.H.I.E.L.D. and its members.

title: Ant-Man
description: Follows Scott Lang, a former thief trying to rebuild his life, who is recruited by scientist Hank Pym to become the new Ant-Man and protect his shrinking technology from falling into dangerous hands. Introduces the Pym Particles and the science behind shrinking and growing. Explores Hank Pym's history as the original Ant-Man and his connection to S.H.I.E.L.D.'s early years. Introduces Darren Cross (Yellowjacket), a former protégé of Hank's who attempts to weaponise shrinking technology for his own purposes.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Three, Episodes 1 - 19
description: Continues Coulson's mission to rebuild S.H.I.E.L.D. as the organisation faces a new global challenge: the emergence of more Inhumans around the world. Expands the Inhuman storyline by exploring the growing number of enhanced individuals, their origins, and the struggle between protecting them and controlling them. Introduces Hive, a powerful ancient Inhuman threat whose arrival creates one of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s most dangerous conflicts. Shows S.H.I.E.L.D. evolving into a more secretive and advanced organisation, operating in the shadows while governments remain suspicious after the Hydra crisis.

title: Captain America: Civil War
description: Follows the Avengers as they are forced to confront the consequences of their actions, leading to a conflict over whether superheroes should be controlled by governments. Divides the Avengers into two opposing sides: Team Captain America, who believe heroes must remain free to act when necessary, and Team Iron Man, who believe accountability and oversight are needed. Introduces Tom Holland's Spider-Man into the MCU, establishing his connection with Tony Stark. Introduces T'Challa (Black Panther), the prince of Wakanda, whose search for revenge leads him into the conflict while beginning his own heroic journey. Reveals the truth behind the Winter Soldier and his connection to Steve Rogers, while exploring themes of friendship, loyalty, and forgiveness. Has huge consequences for the MCU, breaking apart the Avengers and changing the relationships between heroes. Transforms the Avengers from a united team of heroes into fractured individuals dealing with the consequences of their choices.

title: Black Widow
description: Follows Natasha Romanoff as she goes on the run after the Avengers split, forcing her to confront her past and the organisation that created her: the Red Room. Explores Natasha's history as a trained assassin and her complicated relationship with the other Black Widows who were raised alongside her. Introduces Yelena Belova, Natasha's "sister" figure and fellow Black Widow, as well as Red Guardian and Melina Vostokoff, Natasha's forgotten family. Reveals more about the Red Room programme, showing how the Black Widows were controlled, manipulated, and trained into weapons.

title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
description: Follows Peter Parker as he returns to his normal life after fighting alongside the Avengers, struggling to prove himself as more than just a kid with powers. Explores Peter's early days as Spider-Man in the MCU, as he balances school, friendships, and protecting his neighbourhood from everyday threats. Introduces Adrian Toomes (Vulture), who uses advanced alien technology left behind after the Battle of New York to create weapons. Expands Peter's connection with Tony Stark, showing Tony acting as a mentor while Peter learns that being a hero is about responsibility rather than recognition.

title: Black Panther
description: Follows T'Challa as he returns to Wakanda following his father's death, taking on the responsibility of becoming king while protecting his nation's secrets. Expands the MCU with Wakanda, one of the world's most advanced civilisations, hidden behind a powerful isolationist policy. Explores the legacy of Wakanda and the question of whether its technology and resources should be shared with the rest of the world. Introduces Erik Killmonger, a powerful and skilled warrior whose personal history with Wakanda challenges T'Challa's beliefs about leadership and justice. Expands the MCU's political and cultural side through Wakandan technology, the Dora Milaje, Vibranium, and the traditions surrounding the Black Panther mantle.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Three, Episodes 20 - 22
description: Continues the fallout from the Inhuman crisis as Coulson and his team face the consequences of their choices and the growing threat posed by Hive. Explores the dangers of enhanced individuals being manipulated and weaponised. Pushes S.H.I.E.L.D. into a new era as the organisation faces major losses, sacrifices, and changes in leadership. Shows the increasing tension between ordinary humans and enhanced people.

title: Daredevil: Season Two
description: Continues Matt Murdock's journey as he struggles to balance his life as a lawyer with his role as Daredevil while crime in Hell's Kitchen evolves. Introduces Frank Castle (The Punisher), a violent vigilante whose brutal methods force Matt to question his own beliefs about justice and punishment. Introduces Elektra Natchios, Matt's former lover and a skilled assassin who pulls him back into a dangerous world connected to his past. Introduces The Hand, a secretive organisation of ninja warriors with ties to ancient conflicts. Develops Matt's internal struggle between being a lawyer, a vigilante, and a man trying to protect the people around him without losing himself.

title: Luke Cage: Season One
description: Follows Luke Cage, a man with superhuman strength and unbreakable skin, as he tries to live a quiet life in Harlem while being pulled into a fight against organised crime. Explores Luke's origins, revealing how experiments gave him his abilities and why he chooses to stay hidden rather than become a public hero. Introduces Cornell (Cottonmouth) Stokes and Mariah Dillard, whose ambitions threaten the community Luke is trying to protect.

title: Deadpool
description: Follows Wade Wilson, a former special forces operative turned mercenary, who undergoes a brutal experiment that gives him accelerated healing while leaving him physically scarred. Explores Wade's transformation into Deadpool, a violent but humorous anti hero who uses his abilities to hunt down the people responsible for ruining his life. Introduces X-Men members Colossus and Negasonic Teenage Warhead. Takes place within the X-Men universe but intentionally ignores and jokes about continuity rules. Breaks traditional superhero conventions through fourth-wall humour, self-awareness, and a more mature approach to comic-book storytelling.

title: Doctor Strange
description: Follows Stephen Strange, a brilliant but arrogant surgeon whose life changes after a devastating accident leaves him unable to continue his career. Introduces the mystical side of the MCU, revealing that reality is protected by sorcerers who defend Earth from magical and interdimensional threats. Introduces the Ancient One, Wong, Karl Mordo, and Dormammu, expanding the MCU beyond science and superheroes. Introduces concepts such as alternate dimensions, the Mirror Dimension, astral projection, and manipulation of time through the Eye of Agamotto (the Time Stone). Reveals the Time Stone as one of the Infinity Stones.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Four
chronologicalYear: 2016 (difficult to place in timeline due to Framework reality, but introduces the supernatural so follows Doctor Strange in this timeline)
description: Follows the aftermath of the Sokovia Accords as S.H.I.E.L.D. operates in secret, while the world becomes increasingly suspicious of enhanced individuals. Introduces Robbie Reyes (Ghost Rider), bringing the supernatural side of Marvel into Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Explores the creation of the Life Model Decoy (LMD) programme, expanding on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s advanced technology and raising questions about artificial intelligence and identity. Introduces the Framework, a virtual reality world that forces the team to confront alternate versions of themselves and the consequences of different choices. Develops Coulson and the team's personal journeys as they deal with loss, guilt, and loyalty. Blends espionage, supernatural horror, science fiction, and psychological drama.

title: Team Thor: One Shot, Part One
description: Follows Thor as he spends time away from the Avengers, living a quiet life in Australia. Introduces Thor's roommate Darryl Jacobson, who struggles to deal with Thor's unusual habits and his attempts to solve the "big questions" of the universe from home. Provides an explanation for Thor's absence during Captain America: Civil War. Shows Thor researching the Infinity Stones and beginning to suspect that a larger threat is approaching. A mockumentary-style short that fills in a small gap in Thor's story while adding extra context to his whereabouts between Age of Ultron and Ragnarok.

title: Team Thor: One Shot, Part Two
description: Continues Thor's time away from the Avengers, showing his attempt to live a normal life while still investigating the events surrounding the Infinity Stones. Follows Thor's roommate Darryl as he struggles with Thor's increasingly strange behaviour and the challenges of living with a powerful Asgardian. Expands the explanation for Thor's absence during Captain America: Civil War, showing that he was dealing with his own investigation rather than choosing a side in the Avengers' conflict. Further explores Thor's belief that a larger cosmic threat is approaching. Continues the mockumentary style of the first short, focusing more on the contrast between Thor's godlike status and ordinary daily life.

title: Iron Fist: Season One
description: Follows Danny Rand, a billionaire who returns to New York after being presumed dead for years, claiming to be the legendary Iron Fist and protector of K'un-Lun. Explores ancient traditions, martial arts, and the connection between Earth and the hidden city of K'un-Lun. Explores Danny's struggle to balance his responsibilities as a warrior with his desire to reclaim his family's company and understand his place in the world. Introduces the Hand as a major threat, connecting the series to the wider Defenders storyline.

title: The Defenders
description: Brings together Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage, and Iron Fist for the first time as they unite to stop a threat that endangers New York City. Continues the storyline of The Hand, the ancient organisation introduced throughout the shows, bringing their plans and mysterious goals to the forefront. Explores the partnership between four very different heroes, forcing them to overcome their differences and learn how to work as a team.

title: The Punisher: Season One
description: Follows Frank Castle, a former Marine turned vigilante, as he uncovers a conspiracy connected to the death of his family and the events that pushed him into becoming the Punisher. Explores Frank's brutal approach to justice, focusing on revenge, trauma, morality, and the psychological cost of violence. Introduces Billy Russo and develops Frank's connection to his former military life, revealing hidden truths about his past and the people he trusted. Further develops characters including Karen Page from Daredevil, while showing the consequences of vigilante actions. Examines whether Frank Castle is a hero, a villain, or a man consumed by his own war.

title: Jessica Jones: Season Two
description: Follows Jessica Jones as she attempts to investigate the origins of her powers and the experiments that created her. Explores Jessica's past and the source of her abilities, revealing more about the accident that changed her life and the people connected to it. Focuses on Jessica's struggle with identity, family, and whether she is defined by her trauma or by the choices she makes afterwards. Further develops Jessica's relationships with Trish Walker, Malcolm Ducasse, and Jeri Hogarth, showing how their choices are affected by Jessica's powers and past.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Five, Episodes 1 - 11
description: Follows Coulson and his team after they are mysteriously transported into the future, where they discover a broken Earth controlled by a powerful alien civilisation. Explores a future where Earth has been destroyed, forcing the team to uncover what caused the disaster and whether they can prevent it from happening in their own time. Introduces new threats and allies while exploring the consequences of the team's previous actions and the possibility of changing fate itself.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
description: Follows Thor as he is forced into a battle for survival on the alien planet Sakaar, while Asgard faces destruction from the Goddess of Death, Hela, who returned to claim Asgard and challenges Thor's understanding of his own power, legacy, and family history. Expands the cosmic side of the MCU by returning to Sakaar, introducing the Grandmaster and the Valkyrie. Develops Hulk's story after Avengers: Age of Ultron, revealing what happened to Bruce Banner after disappearing on the Quinjet and showing a new side of the Hulk.

title: Team Darryl: One Shot
description: Follows Darryl Jacobson after Thor leaves Australia, as he moves to Los Angeles and attempts to find a new roommate to help pay rent. Introduces Darryl's new roommate, the Grandmaster, who has left Sakaar following the events of Thor: Ragnarok and tries to adjust to life on Earth. Explores the comedic contrast between the Grandmaster's extravagant personality and Darryl's ordinary lifestyle. Provides a follow-up to the Team Thor shorts, explaining what happened to Darryl after Thor's departure.

title: Inhumans
description: Follows the Inhuman Royal Family of Attilan after a coup threatens their society, forcing them to flee to Earth and fight to protect their people. Expands on the Inhuman mythology introduced in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., exploring the hidden civilization of Attilan and the traditions of the Inhuman Royal Family. Introduces key characters including Black Bolt, Medusa, Crystal, Karnak, Gorgon, and Maximus. Explores the conflict between the Inhumans who wish to preserve their ancient hierarchy and those who want change and equality.

title: The New Mutants
flashbacks: The pasts of Dani Moonstar, Illyana Rasputin, Rahne Sinclair, Sam Guthrie, Roberto da Costa, and Cecilia Reyes
description: Follows a group of young mutants held in a secret facility where they must confront both their emerging abilities and their own personal fears. Focuses on five young mutants: Dani Moonstar, Rahne Sinclair, Illyana Rasputin, Sam Guthrie, and Roberto da Costa, as they discover the truth behind the facility they are trapped in. Explores a darker, horror-inspired side of the X-Men universe, focusing on trauma, fear, and the psychological effects of having mutant abilities.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Five, Episodes 12 - 22
description: Continues Coulson's teams fight to prevent the future they witnessed, as they return to the present and attempt to stop the destruction of Earth from occurring. Explores the consequences of the team's actions as they discover that changing the future may come with unexpected costs and that some events may be harder to avoid than they thought. Develops the conflict surrounding Graviton, as the team faces a threat connected to the manipulation of gravity and the potential destruction of the planet. Expands the show's exploration of Inhumans, alien technology, and the consequences of creating powerful individuals who can change the course of history. Continues the season's themes of fate, sacrifice, and free will as Coulson and the team must decide whether saving the world is worth personal losses. Takes place during the same general era as Avengers: Infinity War, with the show existing alongside the larger MCU events while focusing on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s own battles away from the Avengers.

title: Luke Cage: Season Two
description: Follows Luke Cage as he embraces his role as Harlem's protector while struggling with the responsibility and consequences that come with being a public hero. Explores Luke's changing relationship with power, as he questions whether simply stopping criminals is enough to create lasting change. Introduces new threats including John McIver (Bushmaster), a skilled fighter with a personal connection to Harlem's history and a desire for revenge against the Stokes family. Continues the aftermath of The Defenders, showing how Luke and other street-level heroes deal with the consequences of working together against larger threats. Further develops Luke's relationships with Claire Temple, Misty Knight, and the people of Harlem.

title: Iron Fist: Season Two
description: Follows Danny Rand as he continues protecting New York while trying to prove himself as the true Iron Fist and understand what his role as a warrior really means. Explores Danny's growth as he moves away from his impulsive approach, learning that being the Iron Fist requires more than just martial arts skill. Explores the history, legacy, and responsibilities connected to the title of the Iron Fist. Develops the aftermath of The Defenders, including the impact of the Hand's defeat. Further develops Danny's relationships with Colleen Wing, Ward Meachum, and other allies while introducing new conflicts within the criminal underworld.

title: Daredevil: Season Three
description: Follows Matt Murdock after his near-death experience, as he returns to Hell's Kitchen physically and emotionally broken while questioning whether Daredevil is truly worth becoming again. Explores the consequences of The Defenders, showing how Matt deals with the aftermath of being trapped beneath Midland Circle and presumed dead by those closest to him. Brings back Wilson Fisk (Kingpin), whose return to power threatens to destroy Matt's life and reputation while allowing Fisk to manipulate the system from within. Introduces Benjamin Poindexter (Bullseye), an FBI agent whose skills and instability make him a dangerous weapon in Fisk's plans.

title: Spider-Man: Into The Spider Verse
description: Follows Miles Morales, a teenager from Brooklyn who becomes Spider-Man after being bitten by a genetically altered spider and must learn what it means to be a hero. Introduces multiple versions of Spider-Man from across the multiverse, including Peter Parker, Spider-Gwen, Spider-Man Noir, Peni Parker, and Spider-Ham. Explores the concept of the Spider-Verse, establishing that multiple realities can contain different versions of the same heroes. A visually unique animated superhero story that reimagines Spider-Man through Miles Morales.

title: Deadpool Two
description: Follows Wade Wilson as he faces a personal tragedy and forms the team known as X-Force while protecting a young mutant from the time-travelling soldier, Cable, a cybernetic soldier from the future who travels back to stop an event that will have devastating consequences. Continues Deadpool's self-aware approach to the X-Men franchise, openly acknowledging and mocking the confusing continuity of the Fox films.

title: Venom
description: Follows Eddie Brock, an investigative journalist whose life falls apart after exposing the wrong people, leading him to bond with the alien symbiote Venom. Introduces the symbiotes, alien organisms that bond with hosts and enhance their physical abilities while influencing their behaviour. Explores the arrival of the Life Foundation's symbiote research, led by Carlton Drake, and the threat posed by the alien species coming to Earth.

title: Ant-Man and The Wasp
description: Follows Scott Lang as he serves the final days of his house arrest after Captain America: Civil War, while reconnecting with Hope van Dyne and Dr. Hank Pym to rescue Janet van Dyne from the Quantum Realm. Introduces Hope as the Wasp, continuing her journey toward becoming a superhero in her own right. Explores the Quantum Realm in greater detail, revealing that it contains unexplored dimensions and possibilities. Introduces Janet van Dyne, the original Wasp, and reveals the consequences of her decades trapped in the Quantum Realm. Introduces Ghost (Ava Starr), a character whose unstable phasing abilities are connected to quantum experiments and who has her own complicated motivations. Post-credits scenes showing the impact of Thanos' Snap on Scott's world.

title: The Avengers: Infinity War
description: Follows the Avengers and their allies as they unite to stop Thanos from collecting all six Infinity Stones and using them to reshape the universe. Reveals Thanos' plan to gather the Infinity Stones and complete the Infinity Gauntlet. Brings together nearly every corner of the MCU, including the Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, Doctor Strange, Spider-Man, Black Panther, and Wakanda. Explores the consequences of the Avengers' split after Captain America: Civil War, with heroes forced to work together despite their broken relationships.

title: The Punisher: Season Two
description: Follows Frank Castle as he attempts to leave his violent past behind, only to be pulled back into conflict when a young girl becomes the target of a dangerous conspiracy. Explores Frank's struggle between trying to live a normal life and accepting that violence is the only way he knows how to protect others. Continues the fallout from Season 1 by bringing back Billy Russo, whose injuries and trauma transform him into the vigilante enemy known as Jigsaw.

title: Jessica Jones: Season Three
description: Follows Jessica Jones as she continues working as a private investigator while facing a new threat from a highly intelligent and dangerous enemy. Explores Jessica's struggle to define herself beyond her trauma, powers, and past experiences, while questioning what kind of hero she wants to be. Introduces Gregory Sallinger, a skilled criminal who challenges Jessica not through superpowers, but through manipulation, strategy, and obsession. Further develops Trish Walker's journey as she gains abilities of her own and takes a very different approach to what it means to fight crime.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Six
description: Follows the S.H.I.E.L.D. team one year after the events of Season 5 as they deal with the loss of Phil Coulson. Introduces Sarge, an alien leader who looks identical to Coulson but has a completely different personality, forcing the team to confront questions about identity, memory, and whether someone can truly be replaced. Splits the team across Earth and space, with Daisy, Simmons, and others facing cosmic threats while Fitz and Enoch continue their journey through the galaxy. Introduces the Shrike, dangerous alien parasites threatening planets across the universe, and reveals the connection between their invasion and a larger cosmic threats.

title: Agents of Shield: Season Seven
chronologicalYear: various years (1931, 1955, 1973, 1976, 1983, 2019) as a result of the time travel events occurring during Agents of Shield: Season Six
description: Follows the S.H.I.E.L.D. team as they travel through different points in history to stop the Chronicoms from rewriting the timeline and preventing S.H.I.E.L.D. from ever existing. Explores the early history of S.H.I.E.L.D., including its origins, key figures, and the events that shaped the organisation before the modern era. Introduces the Chronicoms as a major threat, with the alien beings using time travel technology to alter history and erase humanity's future. Further develops characters such as Daisy Johnson, May, Mack, Simmons, Fitz, Yo-Yo, and Deke as they face the possibility that their entire history could be erased. Expands the show's approach to time travel and alternate realities, creating a separate branch timeline that operates differently from the main MCU continuity.

title: Venom: Let There Be Carnage
description: Continues the story of Eddie Brock and the alien symbiote Venom as they attempt to coexist while facing a new and more dangerous symbiote threat. Introduces Cletus Kasady and his symbiote Carnage, a darker and more violent counterpart to Eddie and Venom. Explores the connection between hosts and symbiotes, like how different personalities influence their abilities. Follows Eddie's struggle to balance his life as a journalist with the responsibilities and chaos that come from sharing his body with Venom.

title: The Avengers: Endgame
description: Follows the surviving Avengers and their allies as they attempt to undo Thanos' Snap and restore the lives lost during the Blip. Explores time travel and alternate timelines as the heroes revisit history to collect the Infinity Stones before Thanos can use them. Focuses on the personal journeys of the original Avengers, particularly Tony Stark, Steve Rogers, Thor, Natasha Romanoff, and Clint Barton, as they deal with loss, failure, and redemption. The conclusion of the Infinity Saga, bringing closure to many of the MCU's longest-running character arcs.

title: Loki: Season One
description: Follows the 2012 variant of Loki after he escapes during the Avengers' time heist, creating a new branch in reality that leads him to the Time Variance Authority (TVA). Explores the concept of the Sacred Timeline, the TVA, and the idea that countless alternate realities exist outside the normal flow of time. Introduces the concept of variants, showing that different versions of individuals can exist across multiple timelines and realities. Introduces Sylvie, a Loki variant who challenges everything Loki believes about destiny, free will, and the nature of reality.

title: Loki: Season Two
description: Continues Loki's journey as he discovers the TVA has been fundamentally changed and the structure of the timelines is at risk. Explores the consequences of the multiverse being opened, with countless branching timelines now existing beyond the control of the TVA. Expands the concept of time-slipping, allowing Loki to experience different points in the TVA's history as he tries to understand and repair the damage caused to the timeline. Further explores the TVA, revealing more about its origins, its workers, and the truth behind the organisation's mission. Develops the multiversal conflict surrounding He Who Remains, the legacy of the one who controlled the Sacred Timeline.

title: What If…?: Season One, Episodes 1 - 5
chronologicalYear: No set year, branches from different points across the MCU timeline, outside the sacred timeline
description: Follows the Watcher, a cosmic being who observes the infinite realities of the multiverse without interfering, as he explores worlds where major events from MCU history unfolded differently. Expands the MCU's understanding of the multiverse by showing that countless alternate realities exist, each shaped by different choices and outcomes. Explores alternate versions of familiar heroes, including Peggy Carter becoming Captain Carter, T’Challa taking on the role of Star-Lord, and Doctor Strange facing a darker path after losing what mattered most to him. Shows how small changes can completely reshape the fate of worlds, affecting everything from the formation of the Avengers to the rise of cosmic and mystical threats. Introduces the zombie universe created by a quantum virus, establishing the alternate reality that later leads into Marvel Zombies. A major expansion of Marvel’s storytelling, proving that the events of the main MCU timeline are only one version of countless possible realities.

title: Marvel Zombies
chronologicalYear: No set year, directly follows the events of What If...? Season 1 Episode 5: “What If… Zombies?!”
description: Continues the zombie universe introduced in What If...?, exploring a world where a quantum virus has transformed many of Earth's heroes into undead creatures. Follows the surviving heroes as they attempt to survive in a post-apocalyptic world while facing infected versions of some of Marvel's most powerful characters. Develops the stories of surviving characters and introduces new heroes within this universe, showing how different people respond to a world without the protection of Earth's Mightiest Heroes. Builds on the multiverse concepts introduced in What If...?, showing how one alternate decision or event can create an entirely different version of Marvel history. A darker expansion of the What If...? zombie timeline, blending superhero action with horror while exploring the consequences of a world where the heroes became the greatest threat.

title: What If…?: Season One, Episodes 6 - 9
chronologicalYear: No set year, branches from different points across the MCU timeline, outside the sacred timeline
description: Continues following the Watcher as he observes different realities across the multiverse, exploring worlds where familiar heroes experience completely different paths and outcomes. Expands the multiverse further by showing alternate versions of major MCU events, characters, and conflicts that exist beyond the main timeline. Explores realities including a world where Killmonger's actions change the events surrounding Tony Stark and Wakanda, a universe where Thor grows up without the same sense of responsibility, and a reality where Ultron successfully achieves his vision for peace. Shows the increasing scale of alternate threats across the multiverse, including Ultron gaining control of the Infinity Stones and becoming a danger beyond his own universe. Further develops the Watcher's role as an observer who refuses to interfere, while testing the limits of his commitment to remain separate from the events he witnesses.

title: What If…?: Season Two
chronologicalYear: No set year, branches from different points across the MCU timeline, outside the sacred timeline
description: Continues following the Watcher as he observes the infinite realities of the multiverse, exploring new worlds where familiar events unfold in unexpected ways. Expands the multiverse by introducing more alternate versions of MCU characters, showing how different choices create entirely new histories and outcomes. Explores alternate realities including Captain Carter's continued journey, a universe where Nebula becomes a Nova Corps officer, and worlds where characters such as Happy Hogan, Hela, and Peter Quill experience drastically different paths. Further develops the concept of variant characters and alternate histories, showing that heroes and villains can become completely different depending on their circumstances. Continues the Watcher's story as his commitment to observing rather than interfering is challenged by events that threaten the balance of the multiverse. Expands the role of Captain Carter, who becomes one of the Watcher's most trusted allies and a key figure in protecting reality from multiversal threats.

title: What If…?: Season Three
chronologicalYear: No set year, branches from different points across the MCU timeline, outside the sacred timeline
description: Continues following the Watcher as he explores infinite realities across the multiverse, observing worlds where familiar heroes, villains, and events take completely different directions. Expands the scope of the multiverse by introducing new alternate histories and unexpected versions of MCU characters, showing how even small changes can reshape entire realities. Explores alternate scenarios involving characters such as Sam Wilson, Peggy Carter, Agatha Harkness. Continues exploring the consequences of powerful beings, cosmic forces, and major decisions across different universes. Further develops the Watcher's relationship with the realities he observes, continuing the conflict between his duty to remain an observer and the responsibility he feels toward protecting the multiverse. Builds on the wider Multiverse Saga by expanding Marvel's collection of alternate universes and reinforcing that the MCU timeline is only one possibility among countless realities.

title: WandaVision
description: Follows Wanda Maximoff as she creates a mysterious reality in the town of Westview, where she and Vision appear to live an idealised suburban life inspired by classic television sitcoms. Explores Wanda's grief and trauma following the loss of Vision in Avengers: Infinity War, as she struggles to process her pain after the events of Endgame. Introduces the concept of the Hex, a powerful magical barrier that transforms Westview into a constantly changing reality shaped by Wanda's subconscious. Expands the MCU's magical side by exploring Wanda's connection to chaos magic and her potential as one of the universe's most powerful beings. Introduces Agatha Harkness, a powerful witch who helps reveal the true nature of Wanda's abilities. Introduces Wanda and Vision's children, Billy and Tommy, whose existence becomes important to Wanda's future storylines. Has major consequences for the Multiverse Saga, directly setting up Wanda's role in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and expanding the MCU's exploration of magic, variants, and alternate realities.

title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
description: Follows Peter Parker as he struggles with the aftermath of Endgame, the loss of Tony Stark, and the expectations placed on him as one of the world's remaining heroes. Takes Peter and his classmates on a school trip across Europe, where he encounters a new threat claiming to come from another dimension. Introduces Quentin Beck (Mysterio), a former Stark Industries employee who uses advanced technology and deception to manipulate the world into believing he is a hero. Explores Peter's relationship with Tony Stark's legacy and his journey toward becoming a more independent hero rather than living in Iron Man's shadow. Expands the MCU's exploration of advanced technology, illusions, and public perception of superheroes following the events of the Infinity Saga.

title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
description: Follows Peter Parker after his identity as Spider-Man is exposed to the world, forcing him to seek help from Doctor Strange to restore his normal life. Explores the consequences of tampering with reality as a spell gone wrong causes villains and characters from other universes to cross into the MCU. Brings together villains from previous Spider-Man universes, including versions of characters from the Sam Raimi and Marc Webb Spider-Man films. Introduces the concept of multiple Spider-Man variants existing across the multiverse, bringing together different generations of the character. Expands Doctor Strange's role in the Multiverse Saga, showing the dangers of manipulating reality and the existence of countless alternate universes. Explores Peter's journey through loss, responsibility, and sacrifice as he learns what it truly means to be Spider-Man. Has enormous consequences for the MCU, including changes to Peter Parker's life, the wider public's knowledge of Spider-Man, and the growing instability of the multiverse. A celebration of Spider-Man's cinematic history that bridges multiple universes while delivering a major turning point for Peter Parker within the MCU.

title: Morbius
description: Follows Dr. Michael Morbius, a scientist suffering from a rare blood disorder, as he attempts to cure himself through experimental research involving vampire bats and genetic manipulation. Explores Morbius' transformation into a living vampire, granting him enhanced strength, speed, flight, and a need to consume blood to survive. Introduces Milo Morbius, Michael's childhood friend who undergoes the same experimental treatment and becomes a dangerous reflection of what Morbius could become. Connects loosely to the wider multiverse through its post-credits scenes, which reference the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home and bring Adrian Toomes (Vulture) into Sony's universe. A darker anti hero origin story that explores the line between science, morality, and monstrosity.

title: Shang-Chi and The Legend of The Ten Rings
description: Follows Shang-Chi, a skilled martial artist who has hidden his past, as he is pulled back into the world of his father Wenwu and the mysterious organisation known as the Ten Rings. Explores the history of the Ten Rings, an ancient weapon that grants its wielder immense power and has existed for thousands of years. Introduces Shang-Chi's family, including his sister Xialing and mother Jiang Li, while exploring themes of identity, heritage, and breaking away from a parent's legacy. Expands the mystical side of the MCU by introducing Ta Lo, a hidden realm filled with mythical creatures and ancient powers. Reveals more about the Ten Rings organisation, which has operated throughout history and has connections to the wider MCU dating back to the events of the first Iron Man film.

title: The Falcon and The Winter Soldier
description: Follows Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes as they deal with the aftermath of the Blip, the return of half the world's population, and the question of who should carry Captain America's legacy. Explores Sam's struggle with accepting the Captain America mantle after Steve Rogers chose him as his successor, while confronting the history and responsibility attached to the symbol. Continues Bucky Barnes' journey as he attempts to move forward from his past as the Winter Soldier and make amends for the actions he was forced to commit. Introduces John Walker as the U.S. government's replacement Captain America, exploring the pressure and expectations placed on someone trying to fill Steve Rogers' role. Expands the political side of the MCU by exploring the consequences of the Blip, including displaced communities, global instability, and the rise of groups such as the Flag Smashers.

title: Eternals
description: Follows the Eternals, a group of ancient cosmic beings who have secretly lived on Earth for thousands of years, protecting humanity from their enemies, the Deviants. Explores the history of the Eternals, revealing their origins, their connection to the Celestials, and why they chose not to interfere in many major events throughout human history. Introduces the Celestials as a major cosmic force within the MCU, expanding the universe beyond the Avengers, Guardians, and known alien civilisations. Reunites the Eternals after centuries apart when the Deviants return, forcing them to question their mission, loyalty, and purpose. Expands the MCU's cosmic mythology by introducing concepts such as the Emergence, ancient alien influence on Earth, and the greater role of Celestials in shaping life across the universe.

title: Hawkeye
description: Follows Clint Barton as he attempts to spend Christmas with his family, but is pulled into a dangerous conflict when his past as the Ronin catches up with him. Introduces Kate Bishop, a young and talented archer who becomes Clint's unlikely partner and begins her journey toward becoming a new generation of hero. Explores the consequences of Clint's actions as Ronin during the Blip, including the enemies he created while hunting criminals after losing his family. Develops Clint's character by focusing on his guilt, trauma, and desire to leave his violent past behind while helping Kate find her own path. A grounded holiday action series that explores legacy, mentorship, and the transition from the original Avengers to a new generation of heroes.

title: Logan
chronologicalYear: 2029 (later timeline placement as it is needed to understand the opening of 'Deadpool and Wolverine')
description: Follows an older, weakened Logan (Wolverine) as he lives a quiet life away from the world of superheroes, caring for an aging Charles Xavier while trying to escape his violent past. Explores the decline of mutant-kind, revealing that new mutants have not naturally appeared for years and that the remaining mutants are being hunted. Introduces Laura Kinney (X-23), a young mutant with abilities connected to Wolverine, forcing Logan to confront his role as a protector once again. Continues the stories of Wolverine and Professor X while showing the physical and emotional consequences of their years of fighting. Acts as a standalone conclusion to Hugh Jackman's portrayal of Wolverine, separate from the main X-Men timeline and the wider MCU. A grounded, emotional farewell to one of Marvel's most iconic characters, exploring what happens when a hero who has spent his life fighting finally reaches the end of the road.

title: Deadpool and Wolverine
earth: Earth-10005, Earth-616, multiple other Earths (designations currently unconfirmed)
description: Follows Wade Wilson (Deadpool) as he is pulled into a multiversal conflict involving the Time Variance Authority (TVA) and an alternate version of Wolverine. Introduces a variant of Logan / Wolverine from another universe, exploring his guilt, failures, and struggle to move beyond the legacy of the Wolverine audiences know. Expands the role of the TVA and the multiverse after the events of Loki, showing how alternate realities are monitored and affected by larger cosmic forces. Brings together characters and concepts from the Fox Marvel universe, including connections to the X-Men films. Explores themes of legacy, redemption, friendship, and what it means for heroes to matter when their worlds are changing. Acts as a bridge between the Fox Marvel universe and the MCU, using the multiverse to revisit characters and timelines. A celebration of Deadpool, Wolverine, and the wider Fox era of Marvel films while moving those characters into the future of Marvel's multiverse storytelling.

title: Kraven The Hunter
description: Follows Sergei Kravinoff as he transforms into the legendary hunter Kraven, driven by a complicated relationship with his father and a desire to prove himself as the world's greatest predator. Explores Kraven's enhanced abilities, gained through a mystical serum and his deep connection to the natural world, making him one of Marvel's most formidable hunters. Introduces key characters from Kraven's mythology, including members of the Kravinoff family and other super-powered adversaries connected to his past. Explores themes of survival, legacy, and revenge as Kraven struggles between embracing his humanity and becoming the ruthless hunter he is destined to be.

title: Spider-Man: Across The Spider Verse
earth: Earth-1610, multiple other universes via Spider Society
description: Continues Miles Morales' journey as Spider-Man as he struggles with his responsibilities while discovering the wider network of Spider-People across the multiverse. Expands the Spider-Verse by introducing the Spider Society, a group of Spider-People from countless realities who protect the stability of the multiverse. Introduces and develops numerous alternate Spider-Man variants, including Miguel O'Hara (Spider-Man 2099), Spider-Woman, and others. Explores the idea of canon events and the choices involved in protecting the multiverse, challenging Miles' beliefs about fate and heroism.

title: Echo
description: Follows Maya Lopez as she returns to her hometown in Oklahoma after the events of Hawkeye, confronting her past, her family history, and the criminal empire she was once part of. Explores Maya's journey after breaking away from Wilson Fisk (Kingpin), as she attempts to reconnect with her Choctaw heritage and discover where she truly belongs. Continues the story of Kingpin after Hawkeye, showing his survival and his efforts to rebuild his criminal organisation. Expands the street-level side of the MCU by exploring Maya's family history, Indigenous heritage, and the legacy of her ancestors. Introduces more supernatural elements through Maya's connection to her ancestral powers, adding a mystical layer to the grounded crime stories of the Defenders era. A grounded crime drama focused on family, identity, trauma, and reclaiming one's own story

title: Doctor Strange In The Multiverse of Madness
flashbacks: America Chavez's childhood, Sinister Strange's childhood
earth: Earth-616, Earth-838, the Gap Junction (interdimensional location), multiple other Earths (designations currently unconfirmed)
description: Follows Doctor Strange as he confronts the dangers of the multiverse after encountering America Chavez, a teenager with the ability to travel between universes. Explores the consequences of Strange's actions in manipulating reality and the growing instability of the multiverse. Sees Strange seek help from Wanda Maximoff, unaware that she has become corrupted by the Darkhold and is pursuing America's powers. Takes Strange and America across multiple alternate realities, where they encounter an alternate version of the Illuminati. Introduces alternate versions of familiar characters, including Captain Carter, Captain Marvel, Black Bolt, Reed Richards and Professor X. Expands the concept of incursions, establishing the potentially catastrophic consequences of universes colliding with one another. Explores Wanda's grief and obsession with reuniting with her children, leading her to use the Darkhold to manipulate the multiverse. Sees Strange confront alternate versions of himself, including Sinister Strange, forcing him to confront the consequences of his own choices. Ends with Strange using the Darkhold to dreamwalk across the multiverse, before confronting the consequences of its use. Concludes with Strange developing a third eye after being exposed to the Darkhold, setting up further consequences for his character.

title: Moon Knight
description: Follows Steven Grant, a mild-mannered museum worker who discovers he shares a body with Marc Spector, a mercenary suffering from dissociative identity disorder and connected to the Egyptian god Khonshu. Explores Marc's life as Moon Knight, a supernatural vigilante empowered by Khonshu to protect travellers of the night and punish those who have escaped justice. Introduces the Egyptian gods and the hidden world of divine beings within the MCU. Introduces Arthur Harrow, a former follower of Khonshu who seeks to unleash the goddess Ammit and judge humanity before crimes are committed. Explores themes of identity, trauma, memory, and healing through Marc and Steven's struggle to understand each other and work together.

title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
description: Follows the people of Wakanda as they mourn the death of King T'Challa while facing new threats from outside forces seeking access to the nation's vibranium resources. Explores Wakanda's struggle to continue without its king, with Shuri, Queen Ramonda, M'Baku, Okoye, and the Dora Milaje each dealing with grief and the responsibility of protecting their nation. Introduces Namor and the underwater kingdom of Talokan, expanding the MCU's world-building by introducing another hidden civilisation with its own history, culture, and connection to Vibranium. Explores Shuri's journey as she confronts her grief and discovers what it means to carry the legacy and power of the Black Panther. Expands the political side of the MCU by showing the growing tension between nations competing for access to rare resources and enhanced technology. A story about loss, legacy, and rebuilding, showing how heroes and nations move forward after devastating change

title: She-Hulk
earth: Earth-616, real-world (She-Hulk exits the Disney+ interface and enters Marvel Studios production / real-world space to confront K.E.V.I.N)
description: Follows Jennifer Walters, a lawyer specialising in superhuman cases, whose life changes after she gains Hulk-like abilities following an accident involving her cousin Bruce Banner. Explores Jennifer's struggle to balance her career, personal life, and new responsibilities as a superhero. Introduces and develops new characters within the superhero legal world, including Emil Blonsky (the Abomination) and other enhanced individuals navigating life after becoming publicly known. Explores the consequences of superheroes existing within everyday society, including legal issues, public attention, and the impact of extraordinary abilities on ordinary life.
